implementation: Produce top-level policy + topic-specific policies (Access, AUP, Data Classification, BYOD, Crypto, Incident, BCP, Vulnerability). Annual review + management approval signature.
references: Auditor checks version history, management approval, and distribution logs.
minimumEvidence: Signed policy docs, version control table, staff communication logs.

implementation: Define responsibilities across all roles (CISO, IT, HR, Legal, Asset Owners) in job descriptions and RACI matrix.
references: Auditor interviews 2-3 role holders outside IT to test security awareness.
minimumEvidence: ISMS RACI matrix, job descriptions with security clauses.

implementation: Separate incompatible duties (request vs approve, dev vs prod deploy, backup runner vs verifier, 2-person finance approval).
references: Auditor checks role segregation policy and system workflow configs.
minimumEvidence: Segregation of duties policy, IAM role configs, approval logs.

implementation: Ensure line managers actively enforce security, perform inductions, and escalate security concerns.
references: Auditor interviews non-IT line managers regarding their security duties.
minimumEvidence: Manager KPI objectives, signed induction logs, escalation records.

implementation: Maintain Contacts Register (CERT, DPA, Law Enforcement, Sector Regulators, Emergency Services) with clear contact owners.
references: If a major incident happened tonight, who would you call and who is authorized?
minimumEvidence: Authority Contacts Register with annual review date.

implementation: Maintain active memberships in security forums, ISACs, vendor advisories, OWASP, and NCSC programs.
references: Show me a recent piece of threat intelligence received and what action was taken.
minimumEvidence: Membership register, intelligence logs, actioned security bulletins.

implementation: Establish process to collect, triage, and analyze threat intelligence (OSINT, ISAC, vendors). Produce quarterly reports.
references: Trace how a recent threat intelligence item affected your risk register or controls.
minimumEvidence: Threat Intelligence Register, quarterly threat reports, updated risk entries.

implementation: Embed security gates in SDLC/Project framework (Requirements, Design Threat Model, Pre-launch Pen Test, Post-launch Audit).
references: Auditor picks a recent project and requests security review records.
minimumEvidence: Project security checklist, completed security gate sign-offs.

subcategory: Inventory of information and other associated assets
implementation: Maintain formal Asset Register with ID, name, owner, custodian, classification, location, and lifecycle status.
references: Auditor samples 10 assets and verifies owner, location, and classification.
minimumEvidence: Asset Register covering hardware, software, data, cloud, and paper.

subcategory: Acceptable use of information and other associated assets
implementation: Produce Acceptable Use Policy (AUP) covering IT, email, media, personal devices, and AI tools. Require annual acknowledgement.
references: Auditor requests sample signed AUP and checks enforcement workflow.
minimumEvidence: Signed/acknowledged AUP records, disciplinary link evidence.

implementation: Integrate asset return into HR leaver checklist (laptops, cards, tokens) within 24h of departure.
references: Auditor checks 3 recent leavers for timely asset return records.
minimumEvidence: Completed HR Leaver Checklists with signatures and timestamps.

implementation: Define classification taxonomy (e.g., Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted) with handling rules for each tier.
references: What is the classification of customer data, and how is it handled?
minimumEvidence: Data Classification Policy, handling matrix.

implementation: Apply digital/physical labels according to classification (Purview, Drive labels, header/footers, physical stamps).
references: Auditor inspects sample documents from each tier for proper labeling.
minimumEvidence: Labeled document samples, DLP auto-labeling configs.

implementation: Policy & enforcement for secure file transfer, encrypted email (TLS/Confidential+), hardware-encrypted USBs, and third-party DPAs.
references: How do you transfer customer PII to your payroll processor?
minimumEvidence: Information Transfer Policy, SFTP/TLS configs, signed DPAs.

implementation: Define Access Control Policy (RBAC, deny-default, approval workflows, mandatory review cycles).
references: How is access to system X requested, approved, provisioned, and revoked?
minimumEvidence: Access Control Policy, permission matrix, access tickets.

implementation: Manage full identity lifecycle (Joiner start date, Mover 24h adjust, Leaver 2h disable/30d purge). No shared accounts.
references: Auditor checks for active accounts belonging to former employees.
minimumEvidence: IAM logs, provisioning tickets, zero active leaver accounts.

implementation: Password policy (min 12 chars, no periodic force rotation, breached-pass screening, MFA for remote/privileged access).
references: Auditor checks technical password enforcement in AD/IdP.
minimumEvidence: IdP password policy settings, MFA enforcement reports.

implementation: Formal access reviews: quarterly for privileged accounts, annually for all standard accounts by business asset owners.
references: Auditor reviews last access review for critical system and checks revocations.
minimumEvidence: Signed Access Review reports, revocation change tickets.

implementation: Perform vendor security risk assessments, tier suppliers (Tier 1-3), require ISO 27001/SOC 2 for Tier 1.
references: Auditor requests vendor register and security evidence for highest-risk vendor.
minimumEvidence: Supplier Risk Register, vendor assessment questionnaires, audit certificates.

subcategory: Addressing information security within supplier agreements
implementation: Include standard security schedule/DPA in contracts (data protection, incident reporting 24/72h, audit rights, data deletion).
references: Auditor inspects sample Tier 1 contract for mandatory clauses.
minimumEvidence: Signed vendor contracts containing mandatory security schedules.

subcategory: Managing information security in the ICT supply chain
implementation: Assess supply chain risk (vendor origin, open-source deps, SBOM for critical software, CVE monitoring).
references: What is your process if a critical supplier has a security breach?
minimumEvidence: Supply Chain Risk Assessment, SBOM files, procurement RFPs.

subcategory: Monitoring, review, and change management of supplier services
implementation: Conduct annual supplier reviews (SLA, incident history, cert validity). Assess impact of supplier changes before approval.
references: Auditor asks for evidence of last review for primary cloud provider.
minimumEvidence: Annual Supplier Review reports, SLA tracking, change assessments.

subcategory: Information security for use of cloud services [NEW]
implementation: Cloud Security Policy, Cloud Register (provider, classification, shared responsibility matrix, certs, data residency, exit plan).
references: Who approved cloud service X? Where does data reside? What is exit plan?
minimumEvidence: Cloud Services Register, CSPM reports, exit strategy docs.

subcategory: Information security incident management planning and preparation
implementation: Documented Incident Response Plan (IRP) with P1-P4 tiers, escalation paths, CSIRT roster, and regulatory notification triggers.
references: When was the last IRP test? Walk me through P1 escalation.
minimumEvidence: Incident Response Plan, CSIRT contact list, annual tabletop exercise report.

subcategory: Assessment and decision on information security events
implementation: Establish objective triage criteria (Event vs Incident). Assign triage officer per shift. Log all decisions.
references: Auditor asks to see last 5 logged security events and classification rationale.
minimumEvidence: Event Triage Log, classification criteria document.

implementation: Execute PICERL response model. Document actions with timestamps. Notify regulators within 72h (GDPR) if required.
references: Auditor inspects incident response record from past 12 months.
minimumEvidence: Incident timeline logs, containment records, DPA notification forms.

implementation: Conduct formal Post-Incident Review (PIR) within 5 days for P1/P2. Feed findings into risk register and management review.
references: Show me the PIR report for your last major incident and resulting actions.
minimumEvidence: Post-Incident Review (PIR) reports, 5-Why analysis, updated Risk Register.

implementation: Document Evidence Handling Procedure (chain of custody, write-blockers, forensic imaging, immutable log storage).
references: How do you prove digital evidence was not tampered with?
minimumEvidence: Evidence Handling Procedure, forensic chain of custody logs.

implementation: Integrate security controls into BCP/DR plans. Ensure security remains active during failover.
references: Auditor reviews last DR test report for security control validation.
minimumEvidence: BCP/DR Plans containing security specs, DR test report.

implementation: Conduct BIA defining RTO and RPO for critical ICT services. Test recovery against targets at least annually.
references: What is RTO/RPO for CRM system? What was actual recovery time in last test?
minimumEvidence: Business Impact Analysis (BIA), ICT DR test report with metrics.

subcategory: Legal, statutory, regulatory, and contractual requirements
implementation: Maintain Legal & Regulatory Register (GDPR, NIS2, PCI DSS, local laws) mapping requirements to owners and compliance proof.
references: What laws apply to processing customer PII? Who monitors compliance?
minimumEvidence: Legal Register with regular review timestamps.

implementation: Maintain Software Licence Register. Perform annual SAM audit comparing deployed software against owned licences.
references: When did you last verify compliance with software licences?
minimumEvidence: Software Licence Register, SAM audit report.

implementation: Publish Records Retention Schedule. Implement technical controls preventing early deletion/tampering.
references: Produce management review minutes from 3 years ago.
minimumEvidence: Records Retention Schedule, immutable archive store configs.

implementation: Maintain Article 30 RoPA, conduct DPIAs for high-risk processing, appoint DPO, enforce data minimisation & 30d DSAR response.
references: Show me your RoPA and the last DPIA conducted.
minimumEvidence: Record of Processing Activities (RoPA), DPIA reports, DSAR log.

implementation: Conduct annual independent security review (internal audit by independent auditor, external consultant, or pen test).
references: Auditor checks independence and qualifications of the reviewer.
minimumEvidence: Independent Security Audit Report, reviewer credentials.

subcategory: Compliance with policies, rules, and standards
implementation: Conduct technical compliance audits (CIS Benchmark scans, vulnerability scans, DLP reports) regularly.
references: How do you verify baseline technical configurations are maintained?
minimumEvidence: Technical Compliance Audit reports, CIS benchmark scan logs.

implementation: Produce Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for IT/security operations (backup, patching, IAM, changes, scanning).
references: Auditor selects critical process and checks SOP vs operational records.
minimumEvidence: Version-controlled SOP documents, execution records.

implementation: Tiered background checks (ID, right-to-work, references; DBS/financial for confidential/privileged roles). Re-screen 5 years.
references: What screening did your CISO and database administrator undergo?
minimumEvidence: Screening Policy, HR candidate background check files.

implementation: Contracts must include explicit security clauses (NDA, policy adherence, AUP, incident reporting, asset return).
references: Auditor inspects sample employment contract and contractor agreement.
minimumEvidence: Employment contract templates, signed worker agreements.

subcategory: Information security awareness, education, and training
implementation: Mandatory annual security training (100% completion target), new joiner induction, quarterly phishing simulations.
references: Auditor checks annual training completion rates and phishing click metrics.
minimumEvidence: LMS completion logs, phishing campaign analytics, induction checklists.

implementation: Formal HR disciplinary process for policy violations, applied consistently across all staff levels.
references: Has the disciplinary process been applied for a security breach?
minimumEvidence: HR Disciplinary Policy, sanitized disciplinary case logs.

subcategory: Responsibilities after termination or change of employment
implementation: Leaver process: accounts disabled within 2h/last day, assets returned, privileged access revoked immediately, NDA reminder.
references: Auditor spot-checks 3 recent leavers for exact account disable timestamps.
minimumEvidence: HR Leaver checklist, active directory disable logs.

implementation: Maintain NDA Register. Enforce signed NDAs prior to granting access to confidential data for staff/third parties.
references: Auditor requests NDA Register and checks recent contractor NDA.
minimumEvidence: NDA Register, signed NDA documents.

implementation: Remote Working Policy: managed devices only, full-disk encryption, enforced VPN/ZTNA, auto-lock <=5m, no public Wi-Fi without VPN.
references: Can someone connect from an unmanaged personal laptop? Is VPN enforced?
minimumEvidence: Remote Working Policy, MDM compliance rules, VPN configuration logs.

implementation: Provide effortless reporting tools (email alias, phishing button, Slack channel). Acknowledge within 4h. Track metrics.
references: Auditor asks random employee how they report a suspicious email.
minimumEvidence: Phishing button telemetry, event reporting procedures, response metrics.

implementation: Define security zones. Secure zones (server room): 30m fire doors, electronic access control, opaque/blocked windows, intrusion alarm.
references: Auditor physically inspects server room for locks and perimeter security.
minimumEvidence: Physical Security Policy, site layout diagrams, perimeter alarm logs.

implementation: Electronic badge access, escorted visitor logs, contractor inductions, turnstiles/mantraps. Logs retained 12 months.
references: Auditor checks physical access logs for anomalous entries or leaver access.
minimumEvidence: Visitor Logbooks, electronic access control logs.

implementation: Conduct physical security walk-throughs. Enforce locked cabinets for Confidential documents and auto-locking screens.
references: Auditor conducts office walk-through looking for clear desk/screen violations.
minimumEvidence: Physical Audit checklists, clean desk inspection logs.

implementation: CCTV coverage of secure area entries and server room interior. Retain 30-90 days. Register with DPA. Health checks.
references: Are all CCTV cameras operational today? Show me last health check.
minimumEvidence: CCTV topology map, retention policy, camera health check logs.

subcategory: Protecting against physical and environmental threats
implementation: Physical Risk Assessment. Implement FM200/clean agent fire suppression, raised floors, dual UPS, HVAC redundancy.
references: Auditor checks maintenance contracts and test logs for fire suppression and UPS.
minimumEvidence: Environmental Risk Assessment, UPS/HVAC/Fire maintenance logs.

implementation: Secure area rules: no solo working, escorted visitors, no cameras/recording, clean-up before leaving, monthly log review.
references: Auditor checks access logs to see last non-IT visitor in server room.
minimumEvidence: Secure Area SOP, visitor escort log.

implementation: Technical screen lock (<=5 min timeout via MDM). Clear desk policy for physical confidential documents, paper shredders.
references: Auditor walks office after hours inspecting desks and monitors.
minimumEvidence: GPO/MDM screen lock policy, unannounced spot-check audit logs.

implementation: Server room env monitoring (18-27°C, 40-60% humidity). Hot/cold aisle layout. Monitors angled away from public view.
references: Auditor inspects environmental monitoring dashboard and monitor placement.
minimumEvidence: Environmental sensor logs, data centre layout diagram.

implementation: Mandatory full-disk encryption, encrypted USBs, privacy screens in public, loss reporting <1h, remote wipe enabled.
references: What happens if a laptop is stolen at an airport? How fast is it wiped?
minimumEvidence: MDM Encryption compliance report, stolen device reporting SOP.

implementation: Removable media register. Encrypt Confidential+ data on media. Sanitization/shredding with Certificate of Destruction (CoD).
references: Show me Certificates of Destruction for recently decommissioned media.
minimumEvidence: Media Handling SOP, Certificate of Destruction (CoD) records.

implementation: UPS load testing every 6 months, annual generator failover test, HVAC PM every 6 months, dual power feeds.
references: Auditor asks for last UPS load test report and maintenance logs.
minimumEvidence: Utility maintenance logs, UPS test results, dual-feed SLA.

implementation: Network cables in conduits, labelled patch panels, locked comms cabinets, power/data separation, disable unused ports.
references: Auditor checks comms room cable tidiness and unmapped active port counts.
minimumEvidence: Network cabling schematics, port audit logs.

implementation: Maintenance log for critical hardware. Escort external technicians. Wipe storage before off-site repair.
references: Auditor inspects maintenance log for server room equipment.
minimumEvidence: Hardware Maintenance Log, pre-repair data wipe logs.

subcategory: Secure disposal or reuse of equipment
implementation: Data sanitization per NIST 800-88 (clear/purge/destroy). Obtain signed Certificate of Destruction (CoD) retained 3 years.
references: Auditor checks disposal log and matching CoD certificates.
minimumEvidence: Disposal Register, NIST 800-88 wiping logs, vendor CoD docs.

implementation: MDM enforcement: BitLocker/FileVault, EDR agent, patch SLA, 5m screen lock, no local admin rights, conditional access.
references: Auditor reviews MDM compliance dashboard for non-compliant devices.
minimumEvidence: MDM Compliance Dashboard, Endpoint Configuration baseline.

implementation: Least privilege, Just-In-Time (JIT) PAM access, separate admin accounts, quarterly reviews, break-glass account monitoring.
references: Show me who has Domain Admin rights and when they were last used.
minimumEvidence: PAM access logs, quarterly privileged access review sign-offs.

implementation: RBAC matrix mapped to business roles. Block production access for dev roles. Toxic combination review (maker/checker).
references: Auditor checks permission matrix for segregation of toxic roles.
minimumEvidence: RBAC Matrix, application authorization config screenshots.

implementation: Git repos with access control, branch protection (2 reviewers), secret scanning (pre-commit hooks), read/write separation.
references: Show me who has write access to production repos. Has a secret been committed?
minimumEvidence: Git branch protection settings, secret scanner alerts.

implementation: NIST 800-63B standard: 12+ chars, breached-pass screening, lockout after 10 attempts, mandatory MFA (FIDO2 preferred for admin).
references: Auditor inspects technical IdP settings for password and MFA rules.
minimumEvidence: IdP Authentication Policy config, MFA enrollment report.

implementation: Monitor CPU/RAM/Disk/Network. Alert at 70%, remediate at 85%. 12-month capacity forecasting. Monitor cloud spend spikes.
references: How do you know 90 days in advance that storage needs expansion?
minimumEvidence: Capacity Monitoring Dashboard, quarterly capacity forecast reports.

implementation: EDR on all endpoints, email sandbox/anti-phishing gateway, web proxy filtering, app allowlisting on servers.
references: Auditor requests EDR coverage report and details on last malware threat.
minimumEvidence: EDR Central Console report, email gateway quarantine logs.

implementation: Weekly external / monthly internal authenticated vulnerability scans. SLAs: Critical 24-72h, High 7d, Med 30d. Monitor CISA KEV.
references: How many critical vulnerabilities are open right now and for how long?
minimumEvidence: Vulnerability Scan reports, remediation tracking register, risk sign-offs.

implementation: Harden systems using CIS Benchmarks / STIGs. Deploy via automation (Ansible/Terraform). Detect drift via CSPM.
references: What is your configuration baseline for Windows Server / Cloud?
minimumEvidence: CIS Benchmark compliance reports, Ansible/Terraform baseline scripts.

implementation: Automated deletion at end of retention. Purge backup sets. Certified cloud object deletion. Quarterly audit report.
references: If a customer requests erasure under GDPR, how do you purge backup sets?
minimumEvidence: Data Deletion SOP, automated purge job logs, deletion audit report.

implementation: Mandatory data masking/anonymization/tokenization in dev/test environments. No raw production PII in non-prod.
references: Show me customer data records in your development database.
minimumEvidence: Data Masking SOP, anonymization script configs, dev database export logs.

implementation: DLP at Endpoint, Network/Proxy, and Cloud (CASB). Block unauthorized USB copies, email exfiltration, or unapproved cloud uploads.
references: How would you know if an employee emailed customer PII to personal Gmail?
minimumEvidence: DLP Policy configuration, DLP incident triage log.

implementation: 3-2-1-1 backup strategy (1 offline/immutable). Daily backup, quarterly test restoration to isolated environment with metrics.
references: When was the last restoration test? Did it meet target RPO/RTO?
minimumEvidence: Backup schedule configs, quarterly restoration test log with timings.

implementation: Multi-AZ/region cloud design, active-active or active-passive failover, load balancing, annual failover simulation test.
references: Show me failover architecture and the results of the last failover test.
minimumEvidence: High Availability architecture diagram, failover test report.

implementation: Centralized logging (auth, admin actions, data access, firewalls). Retain 12m online / 24m archive. Write-once/immutable storage.
references: Can you pull all auth logs for user X for the past 90 days right now?
minimumEvidence: Log Management Policy, SIEM ingestion coverage report, log integrity proof.

implementation: SIEM (Sentinel/Splunk) real-time detection rules (brute force, impossible travel, mass download). Defined alert response SLAs.
references: Show me the last 3 SIEM alerts and their triage resolution notes.
minimumEvidence: SIEM alert dashboard, incident triage queue, monthly rule tuning logs.

implementation: NTP synchronization against trusted source (pool.ntp.org). Max drift <=1s (<=0.1s crypto). Alert on drift >5s.
references: Can you correlate logs across firewall, SIEM, and EDR with timestamp confidence?
minimumEvidence: NTP server configuration, NTP drift monitoring alerts.

implementation: Restricted list of admin utilities (PsExec, Nmap, Sysinternals). Block execution via app control; log all executions via SIEM.
references: Is PowerShell remoting enabled across servers? How is its use monitored?
minimumEvidence: AppControl allowlist policy, SIEM Event ID 4688 logs.

subcategory: Installation of software on operational systems
implementation: Application allowlisting (AppLocker/WDAC) on servers. Standard users cannot install endpoint software. CASB for Shadow IT.
references: Can standard users install software or browser extensions on laptops?
minimumEvidence: AppLocker policy file, IT software deployment log, CASB Shadow IT report.

implementation: Network diagram, stateful firewalls (default-deny), IDS/IPS, egress filtering, NAC for network access, annual rule review.
references: Auditor inspects network architecture map and firewall rule review log.
minimumEvidence: Network Topology diagram, firewall rule review records, NAC logs.

implementation: SLA security clauses for ISP/SD-WAN providers (DDoS mitigation, uptime, breach notice). Annual failover testing.
references: What DDoS mitigation commitments exist in your ISP contract?
minimumEvidence: Network Service Contracts, ISP SLA reports, WAN failover test log.

implementation: VLANs with firewall routing (Users, Servers, Management, Guest, BYOD, IoT). Strict inter-VLAN ACLs.
references: Show me firewall rules between User VLAN and Production Server VLAN.
minimumEvidence: VLAN architecture map, firewall inter-VLAN routing rules.

implementation: Secure Web Gateway (SWG) / DNS filtering blocking malware, phishing, proxy, and unauthorized file sharing for remote & office.
references: What happens if a user clicks a malicious link? Is remote traffic filtered?
minimumEvidence: SWG URL filtering policy, web proxy block logs.

implementation: AES-256, RSA-2048+, SHA-256+, TLS 1.2/1.3. Disable legacy SSL/TLS/DES. KMS key management with annual rotation.
references: Are TLS 1.0/1.1 disabled on external portals? Show me key management SOP.
minimumEvidence: Cryptography Policy, SSL Labs / testssl.sh scan report, KMS rotation logs.

implementation: Integrate security in SDLC: Threat model -> SAST -> DAST -> SCA -> Container Scan -> Pen Test before release.
references: Auditor picks a recent release and checks security gate pass records.
minimumEvidence: SDLC Security Policy, CI/CD security pipeline build logs, security sign-offs.

implementation: Security Requirements baseline based on OWASP ASVS Level 2 for all bespoke software developments or software procurements.
references: Show me security requirements specified for the customer portal.
minimumEvidence: Application Security Requirements template, completed project specs.

subcategory: Secure system architecture and engineering principles
implementation: Principles: Least privilege, defence-in-depth, fail secure, zero trust, secure defaults. Document trade-offs in ADRs.
references: Show me Architecture Decision Records (ADRs) for major systems.
minimumEvidence: Architecture Decision Records (ADRs), system design blueprints.

implementation: OWASP Top 10 standards, SAST/SCA in CI pipeline, mandatory peer code review, pre-commit secret scanning, parameterised queries.
references: Show me a PR code review catching a security bug or secret scanner setup.
minimumEvidence: Secure Coding Standard, PR review logs, GitHub/GitLab SAST reports.

subcategory: Security testing in development and acceptance
implementation: Automated SAST/DAST/SCA in pipeline + annual third-party penetration test (CREST/CHECK). Criticals block release.
references: Show me the latest penetration test report and remediation tracking.
minimumEvidence: Penetration Test Report, DAST scan logs, vulnerability remediation tracker.

implementation: Contracts require OWASP ASVS L2, code scanning rights, SBOM delivery, vendor SDLC review before engagement.
references: What is your security review process when external developers deliver code?
minimumEvidence: Third-party Dev Contract, delivered SBOM files, code audit report.

subcategory: Separation of development, test, and production environments
implementation: Strict environment segregation. Separate credentials, no dev-to-prod direct connections, no real prod data in dev.
references: Can a developer SSH into production? Is prod data in dev DB?
minimumEvidence: Network ACL rules, deployment pipeline config, IAM access lists.

implementation: Formal Change Requests (CR) with risk assessment, rollback plan, approval, and CAB review. Alert on unauthorized changes.
references: Auditor selects recent production deployment and inspects CR record.
minimumEvidence: Change Management Tickets (Jira/ServiceNow), CAB meeting minutes.

implementation: Use synthetic or masked production data for testing. Prohibit raw production data without explicit CISO approval.
references: What data is stored in the development database?
minimumEvidence: Test Data Management Policy, synthetic data generator scripts.

subcategory: Protection of information systems during audit testing [NEW]
implementation: Rules of Engagement (ROE) for audit tools, read-only accounts, scope agreement, exclusion of fragile systems, SIEM logging.
references: Show me written authorization and ROE for the last penetration test.
minimumEvidence: Audit Rules of Engagement (ROE), signed penetration test agreement.
